headline.h0: every 25 C RED verdict is invariant over 5-40 C under Hansen's own temperature law

headline_result.interpretation: amphora-solvency-score ships a Hansen RED verdict built from 25 C parameter tables and an interaction radius R that carries no temperature argument, yet marine two-part epoxy-amine coatings are applied near 5 C and serviced near 40 C. Applying Hansen & Beerbower's own published temperature law (1971; zero fitted parameters) across that envelope: the 25 C baseline reproduces the shipped 67/75 headline exactly and the law implementation matches the published derivatives to 0.0 relative error. H0 (verdict invariance) is REFUTED: worst case 5 of 75 verdicts flip inside 5-40 C, with max |dRED| 0.392252. Where the refutation does and does not rest on alpha is stated precisely: the assumption-free lower bound (S0 -- the alpha-independent 1.22e-3 hydrogen-bonding term acting alone, no thermal-expansion coefficient assumed) flips 0 verdicts, so the H-bonding term BY ITSELF does not refute H0; thermal expansion is necessary. But the refutation is not sensitive to WHICH alpha: invariance already breaks at alpha = 0.000261 1/K, far below any real organic liquid, and the common-alpha flip count is constant at [2] across the entire declared 6.0e-4 .. 1.5e-3 1/K range -- so no alpha value was tuned to produce the result. At alpha = 1.0e-3 1/K the RED of every pair scales between 0.975033 and 1.034313 of its 25 C value while the rank ordering is essentially preserved (min Kendall tau-b 0.990631, AUROC in [0.94733, 0.952381]) -- i.e. temperature moves the DECISION BOUNDARY, not the ranking. Mechanism: co-scaling R with the polymer's own Hansen-norm contraction (S3) leaves 0 flips, removing 5, which localises the drift to the temperature-invariant R rather than to the parameter law. Practical consequence for solvent selection: a fixed-R 25 C Hansen sphere is systematically more permissive at tropical application temperature and more restrictive in winter application, and the exposure is confined to pairs sitting within a few percent of RED = 1 -- e.g. polyamide-nylon66::dimethylformamide (RED 0.9868 at 25 C) crosses the boundary at 12.13 C and polystyrene::acetone (RED 1.0053) crosses at 29.52 C. Effect size is deliberately not overstated: the paired pinned-seed bootstrap CIs on the change in agreement with the 25 C label set are [-0.04, 0.0] at 5 C and [-0.04, 0.0] at 40 C, both straddling zero, so at n = 75 the AGGREGATE divergence is not resolvable -- the durable finding is the identified boundary-crossing pairs and the fixed-R mechanism, not a headline accuracy change. Note also that the fixture labels are 25 C observations, so off-25 C counts measure divergence from the shipped verdict set, not predictive error. Scope: self-authored CC0 fixture, LOCKED_INTERNAL, CONSTRAINT_ONLY -- this is a self-consistency falsification of the shipped rule, NOT external validation, and it does not re-label any pair.

label_temperature_caveat.note: observed_compatible labels are 25 C observations, so the correct_of_75 counts reported at other temperatures measure DIVERGENCE of the temperature-corrected verdict from the 25 C label set, NOT predictive error at that temperature. No pair is re-labelled and no accuracy claim is made off 25 C.

law_verification.method: central difference h=1e-4 K against the analytic right-hand sides

mechanism.direction: RED = Ra/R falls with rising T when R is held fixed, so a fixed-R Hansen sphere is systematically MORE PERMISSIVE hot and MORE RESTRICTIVE cold than its 25 C calibration
mechanism.question: is the drift an artifact of holding the interaction radius R temperature-invariant while all three HSP components contract?

honest_limitations: The alpha-free lower bound (S0) flips ZERO verdicts: the alpha-independent 1.22e-3 hydrogen-bonding term alone does NOT refute H0. Non-zero thermal expansion is necessary for the refutation.

The refutation is nevertheless not alpha-tuned: invariance breaks at alpha = 0.000261 1/K, far below any real organic liquid, and the common-alpha flip count is constant across the entire declared 6.0e-4 .. 1.5e-3 1/K grid.

Both paired-bootstrap CIs on the change in agreement with the 25 C label set straddle zero, so the AGGREGATE divergence is not statistically resolvable at n = 75. The durable findings are the identified boundary-crossing pairs and the fixed-R mechanism, not a headline accuracy change.
Fixture labels are 25 C observations, so off-25 C counts measure divergence from the shipped verdict set, not predictive error at that temperature.

R is treated as temperature-invariant in S0/S1/S2 because that is what the shipped rule does; S3 shows this is precisely where the drift originates. Whether R should co-scale is not settled by this study and would need external solubility data at two temperatures.
The fixture is self-authored CC0, not an external benchmark.

physical_baseline.integration: exact for constant alpha over the envelope; T0 = 298.15 K
physical_baseline.red_sphere: Hansen 2007 handbook Eq. 1.9, Ra^2 = 4*ddD^2 + ddP^2 + ddH^2, RED = Ra/R
physical_baseline.temperature_law: Hansen & Beerbower 1971 (Kirk-Othmer Suppl. Vol., 2nd ed., pp. 889-910); d(dD)/dT = -1.25 a dD, d(dP)/dT = -0.50 a dP, d(dH)/dT = -(1.22e-3 + 0.50 a) dH

primary_sources: C. M. Hansen, Hansen Solubility Parameters: A User's Handbook, 2nd ed., CRC Press 2007, ISBN 978-0-8493-7248-3 (RED sphere Eq. 1.9; Tables A.1/A.2; Ch. 1 temperature dependence)

C. M. Hansen, A. Beerbower, 'Solubility Parameters', in Kirk-Othmer Encyclopedia of Chemical Technology, Suppl. Vol., 2nd ed., Wiley 1971, pp. 889-910 (origin of the d(dD)/dT, d(dP)/dT, d(dH)/dT relations applied here)

provenance.scope: marine anti-corrosion two-part epoxy-amine (DGEBA epoxy + reference polymers) vs coating-relevant solvents

purpose: Falsification test of the temperature-invariance assumption implicit in amphora-solvency-score's shipped Hansen RED solvency verdict. The shipped rule scores every solvent-polymer pair from 25 C Hansen parameter tables with an interaction radius R that carries no temperature argument, yet marine two-part epoxy-amine coatings are applied near 5 C (ISO 12944-7 / IMO PSPC cold-end practice) and serviced near 40 C on tropical topsides. This harness applies Hansen & Beerbower's own published, zero-free-parameter HSP temperature law across that envelope on the module's CC0-1.0 Phase-0 known-answer fixture (5 polymers x 15 solvents = 75 labelled pairs) and asks whether the 25 C verdict survives its own physics. Three declared scenarios bracket the unknown thermal-expansion coefficient (alpha-free lower bound; common alpha swept 6.0e-4 .. 1.5e-3 1/K; solvent-only alpha) plus a mechanism counterfactual co-scaling R. No alpha value is invented or fitted.

reproducibility.determinism: pure-stdlib, no wall-clock, no unpinned RNG; single pinned-seed paired bootstrap (seed 20260731)
